column3: Lesson one. People want to help, far more than you think.
Notice something. Luffy never even heard her story. He didn't need the reasons. She asked, and that was enough.
Real people are more like that than we expect. In one study, students guessed they would need to ask about twenty strangers, before five agreed to fill out a survey. It took about ten.
Across studies like that, with more than fourteen thousand strangers asked, people underestimated the chance of a yes by about half.
These were small favors, mostly between strangers. But the pattern is steady. We expect a no. We usually get a yes.
The no you're afraid of is mostly in your head.
